items.english: How
items.target: どうやって
items.pronunciation: dō yatte
items.reviewNote: Moved from the Nihongo 101 course (lesson-2) by the 2026-08-24 absorption; see docs/designs/nihongo-absorption-2026-08.md. Placed here because: Lesson 7 asks dou yatte ikimasu ka about transport
items.note: Interchangeable with なんで (nande) from this lesson for asking how someone travels; どうやって (dō yatte) is the everyday choice, while なんで (nande) risks being heard as "why" in casual speech.

items.english: Emma-san came to Japan in 2022.
items.target: エマさんは2022ねんににほんにきました
items.pronunciation: Ema-san wa nisen nijūni-nen ni Nihon ni kimashita
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Vocabulary job: 〜ねん exists only as the 2025ねんに fragment and two bare year cards, never in a sentence.
items.note: A year behaves like any other specific time and takes に (ni), exactly as a month or a day does.
items.ttsText: エマさんはにせんにじゅうにねんににほんにきました

items.english: He's coming on Wednesday.
items.target: すいようびにきます
items.pronunciation: suiyōbi ni kimasu
items.reviewNote: Exercise V.B worked example, answer half. Pairs with gibson-itsu-nihon-ni-kimasu-ka. Shows the day-of-week + に pattern in a reply, which the どようびに fragment card only hints at.
items.scene: answering when Gibson-san is coming to Japan

items.english: Smith-san went home on Sunday.
items.target: スミスさんはにちようびにうちにかえりました
items.pronunciation: Sumisu-san wa nichiyōbi ni uchi ni kaerimashita
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Particle job (に vs no particle): member 1 of a minimal pair whose only difference is the time word and the に it forces. This is the distinction Lesson 6 and Lesson 7 together set up and no card states outright.
items.note: にちようび (nichiyōbi) names a specific day, so に (ni) is required after it.

items.english: It's from the 2nd to the 7th.
items.target: ふつかからなのかまでです
items.pronunciation: futsuka kara nanoka made desu
items.reviewNote: Constructed, using the book's own 9がつふつかからなのかまで dates from Exercise II.C. Vocabulary job: ふつか and なのか had no sentence. Answer half of the pair with w2-ryokou-nannichi-kara.
items.scene: answering what dates the trip runs

items.english: Smith-san is going to Tokyo Station tomorrow.
items.target: スミスさんはあしたとうきょうえきにいきます
items.pronunciation: Sumisu-san wa ashita Tōkyō eki ni ikimasu
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Particle job (に vs へ): member 1 of a minimal pair differing only in that one particle. Both members carry a hint because the English is identical.
items.note: に (ni) is the everyday choice for a destination and the one this lesson uses throughout.

items.english: No, I'm going by bus.
items.target: いいえ、バスでいきます
items.pronunciation: iie, basu de ikimasu
items.scene: answering whether you're going to Tokyo Hotel by taxi

items.english: I'll return to Tokyo on Friday.
items.target: きんようびにとうきょうにかえります
items.pronunciation: kin'yōbi ni Tōkyō ni kaerimasu
items.reviewNote: Target Dialogue, Smith's first reply (second sentence). かえります has no sentence card anywhere in the lesson, and this is the book's own example of the specific-time に from GRAMMAR 1 inside a full sentence.
items.note: Two に (ni) in one sentence doing different jobs: the first marks the time, the second the destination.

items.english: How is Smith-san going to Osaka?
items.target: スミスさんはなんでおおさかにいきますか
items.pronunciation: Sumisu-san wa nande Ōsaka ni ikimasu ka
items.reviewNote: Exercise VII worked example. The existing なんでいきますか is a bare fragment with no subject or destination; this is the full question the book drills. I deliberately left out its answer (くるまでいきます) because バスでいきます already teaches that pattern and いいえ、しんかんせんでいきます above makes a second.

items.english: How is Tanaka-san going to the meeting?
items.target: たなかさんはなんでかいぎにいきますか
items.pronunciation: Tanaka-san wa nande kaigi ni ikimasu ka

items.english: It's on the 3rd.
items.target: みっかです
items.pronunciation: mikka desu
items.reviewNote: Constructed from Exercise VIII alternative 1. Form job: the reply half of the alternative question — you pick one and drop the rest of the sentence.
items.scene: answering whether the meeting falls on the 3rd or the 6th

items.english: Is the meeting on the 3rd or the 6th?
items.target: かいぎはみっかですか、むいかですか
items.pronunciation: kaigi wa mikka desu ka, muika desu ka
items.reviewNote: Constructed from Exercise VIII alternative 1. Form job: the noun1は noun2ですか、noun3ですか pattern is a Key Sentence but the only card for it has no answer card, so the exchange is never completed. Also gives むいか its first sentence.
items.note: Both か (ka) are said with a rising intonation, not just the last one.

items.english: Smith-san isn't going home on Saturday.
items.target: スミスさんはどようびにうちにかえりません
items.pronunciation: Sumisu-san wa doyōbi ni uchi ni kaerimasen
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Form job: negative member of the かえります triad. かえりません appears nowhere in the lesson's own cards.
items.note: Member 2 of the set: ます (masu) becomes ません (masen) and nothing else in the sentence moves.

items.english: I'll go there next Monday.
items.target: らいしゅうのげつようびにそちらにいきます
items.pronunciation: raishū no getsuyōbi ni sochira ni ikimasu
items.reviewNote: Exercise IX worked dialogue, Chan's first line. Exercise IX never became cards. This is the one place the book shows a relative week word narrowed to a specific day, which is exactly the に/no-に decision learners get wrong.
items.note: らいしゅうの (raishū no) + a day of the week behaves as one specific time expression, so it takes に (ni) even though らいしゅう on its own would not.

items.english: He's going by motorbike.
items.target: バイクでいきます
items.pronunciation: baiku de ikimasu
items.scene: answering how Tanaka-san is going to the meeting

items.english: Yes, he's coming.
items.target: はい、きます
items.pronunciation: hai, kimasu
items.scene: answering whether Lopez-san is coming next month, on the 8th

items.english: Is Lopez-san coming next month, on the 8th?
items.target: ロペスさんはらいげつのようかにきますか
items.pronunciation: Ropesu-san wa raigetsu no yōka ni kimasu ka

items.english: I go to work by bus.
items.target: バスでしごとにいきます
items.pronunciation: basu de shigoto ni ikimasu
items.scene: answering how you get to work
items.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Extra questions PDF, question 3 answer. Job: contrasts the で (de) of means against the あるいて (aruite) answer above.

items.english: When is the meeting?
items.target: かいぎはいつですか
items.pronunciation: kaigi wa itsu desu ka
items.reviewNote: Duplicate of kaigi-itsu-q in Lesson 3. Its answer card carries a hint and stands alone.

items.english: The gym's day off is Tuesday.
items.target: ジムのやすみはかようびです
items.pronunciation: jimu no yasumi wa kayōbi desu
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Vocabulary job: かようび was the last weekday with no sentence, and やすみ on its own appears only inside ひるやすみ and なつやすみ.
items.note: やすみ (yasumi) covers any break — a day off, a lunch break, or a school holiday.

items.english: Yes, she's going by subway.
items.target: はい、ちかてつでいきます
items.pronunciation: hai, chikatetsu de ikimasu
items.scene: answering whether Emma-san is also going to Ginza by subway

items.english: The business trip is from next Tuesday to Thursday.
items.target: しゅっちょうはらいしゅうのかようびからもくようびまでです
items.pronunciation: shutchō wa raishū no kayōbi kara mokuyōbi made desu
items.scene: answering when the business trip is, from and to
items.excludedReason: pattern: [event/day range]から[day]までです — The から...までです date-range frame is already taught four times by the source (natsuyasumi, futsuka-nanoka, getsuyoubi-mokuyoubi, omatsuri); this only swaps in a new noun.
items.reviewNote: Excluded by the semantic de-dup pass. Pattern: [event/day range]から[day]までです. The から...までです date-range frame is already taught four times by the source (natsuyasumi, futsuka-nanoka, getsuyoubi-mokuyoubi, omatsuri); this only swaps in a new noun.

items.english: What month is the festival?
items.target: おまつりはなんがつですか
items.pronunciation: omatsuri wa nan-gatsu desu ka
items.reviewNote: Exercise II.A worked example. なんがつ is a bare card with no sentence, unlike なんにち and なんようび which the fill-in-the-blank block already puts in questions.

items.english: Lopez-san didn't come to the office yesterday.
items.target: ロペスさんはきのうかいしゃにきませんでした
items.pronunciation: Ropesu-san wa kinō kaisha ni kimasen deshita
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Form job: きませんでした completes the きます conjugation, which otherwise stops at きました. ロペス is the third of the lesson's unused surnames.
items.note: きのう (kinō) takes no に (ni), the same as きょねん (kyonen) and おととい (ototoi).

items.english: It's on August 19th.
items.target: 8がつ19にちです
items.pronunciation: hachi-gatsu jūku-nichi desu
items.reviewNote: Exercise II.B worked example, answer half. Pairs with tanjoubi-wa-itsu-desu-ka and is the only short month + day date card — the existing dated card is the long from/to travel sentence.
items.ttsText: はちがつじゅうくにちです
items.scene: answering when your birthday is

items.english: How do you get to the station?
items.target: どうやってえきにいきますか
items.pronunciation: dōyatte eki ni ikimasu ka
items.excludedReason: pattern: どうやって[place]にいきますか — Source already drills this frame twice (jimu, shigoto); a third example is padding.
items.reviewNote: Excluded by the semantic de-dup pass. Pattern: どうやって[place]にいきますか. Source already drills this frame twice (jimu, shigoto); a third example is padding.

items.english: The meeting is on the 8th, right?
items.target: かいぎはようかですね
items.pronunciation: kaigi wa yōka desu ne
items.reviewNote: Lifted from SPEAKING PRACTICE 3, Smith's closing line (with かいぎ restored as the topic so the card stands alone). Particle job (ね): introduced in Lesson 6 on one card and never used again.
items.note: ね (ne) asks the listener to confirm something you already believe, unlike か (ka), which asks for information you do not have.

items.english: Smith-san walked home.
items.target: スミスさんはあるいてうちにかえりました
items.pronunciation: Sumisu-san wa aruite uchi ni kaerimashita
items.reviewNote: Exercise VI, alternative 3. The exercise's whole point is that あるいて breaks the transport-で pattern, and the deck teaches あるいて only as an isolated word. The fill-in-the-blank block covers the タクシーで version, so this is the contrast card.
items.note: あるいて (aruite) is the exception to the transport で (de) rule — it already means "by walking", so no で follows it. Compare タクシーでうちにかえりました (takushī de uchi ni kaerimashita).

items.english: The summer vacation is from the 10th to the 20th.
items.target: なつやすみはとおかからはつかまでです
items.pronunciation: natsuyasumi wa tōka kara hatsuka made desu
items.reviewNote: Constructed from the Active Communication prompt about summer vacations. Vocabulary job: とおか and はつか had no sentence.
items.note: はつか (hatsuka) is the 20th and ふつか (futsuka) the 2nd — they sound close but share no counting logic.

items.english: Lopez-san is going back to the United States in November.
items.target: ロペスさんは11がつにアメリカにかえります
items.pronunciation: Ropesu-san wa jūichi-gatsu ni Amerika ni kaerimasu
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Vocabulary job: じゅういちがつ had no sentence. Uses アメリカ from Lesson 1 to give かえります a destination other than うち or とうきょう.
items.note: かえります (kaerimasu) is going back to where you belong, which is why it fits a country you came from.
items.ttsText: ロペスさんはじゅういちがつにアメリカにかえります

items.english: Smith-san is going to Tokyo Station tomorrow.
items.target: スミスさんはあしたとうきょうえきへいきます
items.pronunciation: Sumisu-san wa ashita Tōkyō eki e ikimasu
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Particle job (に vs へ): member 2 of the minimal pair. へ was introduced in Lesson 6 on a single card and is exercised nowhere in this lesson.
items.note: へ (e) is the hiragana he, but it is read e whenever it works as a particle. For a destination it swaps with に (ni) freely.

items.english: I'll go at 10:00.
items.target: 10じにいきます
items.pronunciation: jū-ji ni ikimasu
items.reviewNote: Exercise IX worked dialogue, Chan's reply. Answer half of the pair with nanji-ni-kimasu-ka, and the working version of the 5じに fragment card.
items.scene: answering what time you'll come

items.english: I came in September last year.
items.target: きょねんの9がつにきました
items.pronunciation: kyonen no ku-gatsu ni kimashita
items.reviewNote: Speaking Practice 2, Raja's reply. Answer half of the pair. Combines きょねんの (L6) with a month + に, a combination no card shows.
items.ttsText: きょねんのくがつにきました
items.scene: answering when you came to Japan

items.english: What dates does the trip run from and to?
items.target: りょこうはなんにちからなんにちまでですか
items.pronunciation: ryokō wa nan-nichi kara nan-nichi made desu ka
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Particle job (から / まで) combined with a question word in both slots — the pattern the deck only has for なんじ (nan-ji) in Lesson 3.

items.english: I walk to the gym.
items.target: ジムにあるいていきます
items.pronunciation: jimu ni aruite ikimasu
items.scene: answering how you get to the gym
items.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Beginner 2 Week 1-2 PDF. Job: the answer to the どうやって (dō yatte) question, showing あるいて (aruite) used as a means of going.

items.english: Smith-san is going home on Saturday.
items.target: スミスさんはどようびにうちにかえります
items.pronunciation: Sumisu-san wa doyōbi ni uchi ni kaerimasu
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Form job: the ます/ません/ますか triad for かえります, on one fixed sentence so the transformation is visible. どようび also had no sentence card, only the どようびに fragment.
items.note: A named day is a specific time, so it takes に (ni). Member 1 of a かえります (kaerimasu) / かえりません (kaerimasen) / かえりますか (kaerimasu ka) set on the same sentence.

items.english: Yes, I'm going to the Osaka branch office with Kato-san.
items.target: ええ、かとうさんとおおさかししゃにいきます
items.pronunciation: ē, Katō-san to Ōsaka shisha ni ikimasu
items.reviewNote: Target Dialogue, Smith's first reply. Answer half of the split pair with shucchou-desu-ka. It is also the only card that puts ええ (ē) to work — the ee-yes card is flagged uncertain and is a bare word.
items.scene: answering whether you are going on a business trip

items.english: Are you going to Tokyo Hotel by taxi?
items.target: タクシーでとうきょうホテルにいきますか
items.pronunciation: takushī de Tōkyō Hoteru ni ikimasu ka

items.english: It's on the 8th of next month.
items.target: らいげつのようかです
items.pronunciation: raigetsu no yōka desu
items.reviewNote: Speaking Practice 3, Emma's reply. Answer half of the pair with kaigi-wa-itsu-desu-ka, and the only card showing a relative month combined with a specific date.
items.note: らいげつ (raigetsu) from Lesson 6 attaches to a date with の (no), the same way きょねんの (kyonen no) does.
items.scene: answering when the meeting is

items.english: When is Gibson-san coming to Japan?
items.target: ギブソンさんはいつにほんにきますか
items.pronunciation: Gibuson-san wa itsu Nihon ni kimasu ka
items.reviewNote: Exercise V.B worked example. The deck has ks1-emma-april as a statement but no question that asks when someone comes, which is the exercise's whole point.

items.english: It's in March.
items.target: 3がつです
items.pronunciation: san-gatsu desu
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Vocabulary job: answer half of the pair with w2-ryokou-nigatsu-ka-sangatsu-ka. Hint added because the target drops the topic and because the English sits close to the bare さんがつ card.
items.scene: answering whether the trip falls in February or March

items.english: I go to the station by bicycle.
items.target: じてんしゃでえきにいきます
items.pronunciation: jitensha de eki ni ikimasu
items.scene: answering how you get to the station
items.excludedReason: pattern: [transport]で[place]にいきます — Answer half of the removed どうやって pair, and the transport-place-いきます frame is already well covered by source cards (jitensha-eki, shinkansen).
items.reviewNote: Excluded by the semantic de-dup pass. Pattern: [transport]で[place]にいきます. Answer half of the removed どうやって pair, and the transport-place-いきます frame is already well covered by source cards (jitensha-eki, shinkansen).

items.english: Smith-san went to the department store by bus the day before yesterday.
items.target: スミスさんはおとといバスでデパートにいきました
items.pronunciation: Sumisu-san wa ototoi basu de depāto ni ikimashita
items.reviewNote: Exercise VIII worked example. It is the only sentence in the lesson that stacks time + transport + destination + past tense, and nothing in the deck contrasts the に-less relative time word with the に-taking specific one.
items.note: おととい (ototoi) is a relative time word, so it takes no に (ni) — compare きんようびに (kin'yōbi ni), which does. This is the Lesson 6 rule still holding alongside the new one.

items.english: My birthday is October 9th.
items.target: たんじょうびは10がつここのかです
items.pronunciation: tanjōbi wa jū-gatsu kokonoka desu
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Vocabulary job: ここのか and じゅうがつ each had no sentence, and the month + native-reading-day combination appears nowhere.
items.note: The month comes first and the day second, the reverse of the usual English order.
items.ttsText: たんじょうびはじゅうがつここのかです

items.english: Kato-san is going by Shinkansen too.
items.target: かとうさんもしんかんせんでいきます
items.pronunciation: Katō-san mo shinkansen de ikimasu
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Particle job (は vs も): member 2 of the minimal pair. も has not been used since Lesson 4 and appears on no Lesson 7 card.
items.hint: the "too" version — the particle changes, nothing else does
items.note: も (mo) replaces は (wa) rather than joining it; はも is never said.

items.english: Raja-san, when did you come to Japan?
items.target: ラジャさんはいつにほんにきましたか
items.pronunciation: Raja-san wa itsu Nihon ni kimashita ka
items.reviewNote: Speaking Practice 2, Nakamura's first line. Past-tense version of the same question, and the exact pattern Quiz 2 item 1 tests. Speaking Practice 2 currently has no cards at all.

items.english: The concert is in January next year.
items.target: コンサートはらいねんの1がつです
items.pronunciation: konsāto wa rainen no ichi-gatsu desu
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Vocabulary job: いちがつ had no sentence. Frame chosen to reuse the Lesson 6 relative-year words rather than repeat the birthday frame.
items.note: らいねん (rainen) narrows the month with の (no), the same join as きょねんの (kyonen no) and らいげつの (raigetsu no).
items.ttsText: コンサートはらいねんのいちがつです

items.english: The days off are Saturday and Sunday.
items.target: やすみはどようびとにちようびです
items.pronunciation: yasumi wa doyōbi to nichiyōbi desu
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Particle job (と): both existing examples in this lesson are the "with a person" と, so the listing use had no example here at all.
items.note: This と (to) joins two nouns into a list; the same と (to) means "with" when it attaches a person to a verb.

items.english: How do you get to the gym?
items.target: どうやってジムにいきますか
items.pronunciation: dō yatte jimu ni ikimasu ka
items.note: どうやって (dō yatte) asks by what means, like なんで (nande) in this lesson. どうやって (dō yatte) is the more everyday of the two.
items.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Beginner 2 Week 1-2 PDF, which prints it schematically as どうやって〜にいきますか. Rewritten around ジム (jimu) because a shipped 〜 is not something a person can say.

items.english: It's from Monday to Thursday.
items.target: げつようびからもくようびまでです
items.pronunciation: getsuyōbi kara mokuyōbi made desu
items.reviewNote: Constructed from the Exercise II.C alternatives. Particle job (から / まで) with days of the week rather than clock times. Answer half of the pair with w2-shucchou-itsukara-itsumade.
items.scene: answering how long the business trip runs

items.english: How do you go to work?
items.target: どうやってしごとにいきますか
items.pronunciation: dō yatte shigoto ni ikimasu ka
items.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Extra questions PDF, question 3. Job: the same どうやって (dō yatte) frame with a second destination, so the learner sees a slot rather than a fixed phrase.

items.english: Is Lopez-san coming by airplane too?
items.target: ロペスさんもひこうきできますか
items.pronunciation: Ropesu-san mo hikōki de kimasu ka
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Particle job (も) in question form — the brief asks for at least one question among a particle's examples, and も had none anywhere.

items.english: Kato-san is going by Shinkansen.
items.target: かとうさんはしんかんせんでいきます
items.pronunciation: Katō-san wa shinkansen de ikimasu
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Particle job (は vs も): member 1 of a minimal pair differing only in the particle after かとうさん. Hint added because the paired card has almost the same English.
items.hint: the plain statement, marking the topic
items.note: は (wa) simply presents Kato-san as what the sentence is about.

items.english: On foot
items.target: あるきで
items.pronunciation: aruki de
items.hint: the 〜で (de, "by means of") variant, not the usual form
items.note: A variant of あるいて (aruite). Both mean going on foot, and あるいて (aruite) is the one you will hear.
items.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Beginner 2 Week 1-2 PDF, listed there as an alternative to あるいて (aruite). Worth a look at gate 1: if it is not a form you want to produce, exclude it and keep あるいて (aruite) alone.

items.english: Is Smith-san going home on Saturday?
items.target: スミスさんはどようびにうちにかえりますか
items.pronunciation: Sumisu-san wa doyōbi ni uchi ni kaerimasu ka
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Form job: question member of the かえります triad.
items.note: Member 3 of the set: か (ka) is simply added to the end, with no change to word order.

items.english: Raja-san didn't go back to India last year.
items.target: ラジャさんはきょねんインドにかえりませんでした
items.pronunciation: Raja-san wa kyonen Indo ni kaerimasen deshita
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Form job: かえりませんでした exists on no card, so かえります was missing a quarter of its conjugation.
items.note: The past negative is ませんでした (masen deshita), built the same way as いきませんでした (ikimasen deshita) from Lesson 6.

items.english: Is Pak-san coming to Japan on Thursday?
items.target: パクさんはもくようびににほんにきますか
items.pronunciation: Paku-san wa mokuyōbi ni Nihon ni kimasu ka
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Form job: question member of the きます triad.
items.note: Member 3 of the set — a yes/no question, unlike the いつ (itsu) question the exercises drill.

items.english: Will you go back to India during the summer vacation?
items.target: なつやすみにインドにかえりますか
items.pronunciation: natsuyasumi ni Indo ni kaerimasu ka
items.reviewNote: Speaking Practice 2, Nakamura's second line. かえります appears on no question card, and なつやすみ exists only as a bare noun. インド is from Lesson 1.

items.english: I'm going to Hokkaido during the summer vacation.
items.target: なつやすみにほっかいどうへいきます
items.pronunciation: natsuyasumi ni Hokkaidō e ikimasu
items.reviewNote: Constructed from Speaking Practice 2, where Raja says he is going to Hokkaido instead of home. Particle job (へ): third example, and the only one that is not part of the minimal pair.
items.note: なつやすみ (natsuyasumi) counts as a specific time here, so it takes に (ni) even though it names no date.

items.english: It's in September.
items.target: 9がつです
items.pronunciation: ku-gatsu desu
items.reviewNote: Exercise II.A worked example, answer half. Pairs with omatsuri-wa-nangatsu-desu-ka. Hint added because the target drops the topic and because the English sits close to the bare くがつ vocabulary card.
items.scene: answering what month the festival is

items.english: He comes by train.
items.target: でんしゃできます
items.pronunciation: densha de kimasu
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Vocabulary job: でんしゃ is a bare noun card and appears in no sentence anywhere in the lesson. Answer half of the pair with w2-katou-nande-kaisha-ni-kimasu-ka.
items.scene: answering how Kato-san gets to the office

items.english: The presentation is on the 14th of next month.
items.target: プレゼンはらいげつのじゅうよっかです
items.pronunciation: purezen wa raigetsu no jūyokka desu
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Vocabulary job: じゅうよっか had no sentence, and it is one of the three teens that keeps a native reading.
items.note: じゅうよっか (jūyokka) keeps the よっか (yokka) reading rather than becoming じゅうよんにち.

items.english: Is Emma-san also going to Ginza by subway?
items.target: エマさんもちかてつでぎんざにいきますか
items.pronunciation: Ema-san mo chikatetsu de Ginza ni ikimasu ka

items.english: Smith-san is going to the Tokyo Hotel with Suzuki-san by taxi at 12:00 on Monday.
items.target: スミスさんはげつようびの12じにすずきさんとタクシーでとうきょうホテルにいきます
items.pronunciation: Sumisu-san wa getsuyōbi no jūni-ji ni Suzuki-san to takushī de Tōkyō Hoteru ni ikimasu
items.reviewNote: Exercise X worked example (weekly planner). It is the lesson's culminating sentence and the only one that uses every particle taught so far at once; nothing in the deck goes past two slots. Note that ホテル is currently an excluded vocabulary card, but it appears here inside the book's own example.
items.note: The full slot order this lesson builds to: topic は, time に, companion と, means で, destination に, verb.
items.ttsText: スミスさんはげつようびのじゅうにじにすずきさんとタクシーでとうきょうホテルにいきます

items.english: The summer vacation starts in July.
items.target: なつやすみは7がつからです
items.pronunciation: natsuyasumi wa shichi-gatsu kara desu
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Vocabulary job: しちがつ had no sentence. Particle job too — から without まで is a Lesson 3 pattern that this lesson never revisits with dates.
items.note: から (kara) can stand on its own without まで (made) when only the start matters.
items.ttsText: なつやすみはしちがつからです

items.english: Pak-san is coming to Japan on Thursday.
items.target: パクさんはもくようびににほんにきます
items.pronunciation: Paku-san wa mokuyōbi ni Nihon ni kimasu
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Form job: the ます/ません/ますか triad for きます. もくようび had no sentence card either.
items.note: Two に (ni) in a row doing different jobs: もくようびに (mokuyōbi ni) is the time, にほんに (Nihon ni) the destination. Member 1 of a きます (kimasu) / きません (kimasen) / きますか (kimasu ka) set.

items.english: No, I won't go back.
items.target: いいえ、かえりません
items.pronunciation: iie, kaerimasen
items.reviewNote: Speaking Practice 2, Raja's reply. The biggest single hole in the lesson: かえりません appears on no card, so the learner meets かえります only in the affirmative.
items.note: The negative of かえります (kaerimasu), formed the same way as いきません (ikimasen) from Lesson 6.
items.scene: answering whether you'll go back home for the summer vacation

items.english: Are you going by airplane?
items.target: ひこうきでいきますか
items.pronunciation: hikōki de ikimasu ka
items.reviewNote: Target Dialogue, Nakamura's second line. The lesson teaches transport + で but has no yes/no question using it — only なんでいきますか and bare fragments like バスで.

items.english: What time will you come?
items.target: なんじにきますか
items.pronunciation: nan-ji ni kimasu ka
items.reviewNote: Exercise IX worked dialogue, Smith's first line. なんじ came in Lesson 3 but only ever with です; this is the first time it attaches to a verb with に, and the deck has no card for it.

items.english: Raja-san went back to India last year.
items.target: ラジャさんはきょねんインドにかえりました
items.pronunciation: Raja-san wa kyonen Indo ni kaerimashita
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Form job: past pair for かえります on one sentence. Uses the ラジャ / インド pairing the book itself sets up in Speaking Practice 2.
items.note: きょねん (kyonen) is a relative time word, so no に (ni) follows it — unlike きょねんの9がつに (kyonen no ku-gatsu ni), which names a specific month.

items.english: The No. 3 bus goes there.
items.target: 3ばんのバスがいきます
items.pronunciation: san-ban no basu ga ikimasu
items.reviewNote: Constructed on the model of the Lesson 6 card 6ばんのバスがいきます. Particle job (が): answer half of the pair with w2-dono-basu-ga-kuukou-ni, which the Lesson 6 card had no question to answer.
items.note: The answer keeps が (ga) — swapping in は (wa) would make it sound like a change of subject.
items.ttsText: さんばんのバスがいきます
items.scene: answering which bus goes to the airport

items.english: Are you going on a business trip?
items.target: しゅっちょうですか
items.pronunciation: shutchō desu ka
items.reviewNote: Target Dialogue, line 1 (trimmed of the あ、スミスさん、 opening, since the あ card is excluded from the deck). The lesson's title word しゅっちょう exists only as a bare noun card; this is the question the book actually uses it in.
items.note: A noun + ですか (desu ka) is enough to ask this — no verb is needed. Nakamura asks it because Smith is carrying a suitcase.

items.english: When is your birthday?
items.target: たんじょうびはいつですか
items.pronunciation: tanjōbi wa itsu desu ka
items.reviewNote: Exercise II.B worked example, and one of the two Active Communication tasks the lesson closes on. The deck has たんじょうび as a noun and a fill-in-the-blank なんようび question, but not the open いつ question the book actually drills.

items.english: Pak-san is going to Hokkaido with Kato-san in June.
items.target: パクさんは6がつにかとうさんとほっかいどうにいきます
items.pronunciation: Paku-san wa roku-gatsu ni Katō-san to Hokkaidō ni ikimasu
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Vocabulary job: ろくがつ had no sentence. Particle job as well — と meaning "with" has only two examples in the lesson.
items.note: Slot order: time に (ni), then companion と (to), then destination に (ni), then the verb.
items.ttsText: パクさんはろくがつにかとうさんとほっかいどうにいきます

items.english: Tanaka-san went to Kyoto in December.
items.target: たなかさんは12がつにきょうとにいきました
items.pronunciation: Tanaka-san wa jūni-gatsu ni Kyōto ni ikimashita
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Vocabulary job: じゅうにがつ had no sentence. Past tense, so the month cards are not all locked to the non-past.
items.ttsText: たなかさんはじゅうにがつにきょうとにいきました

items.english: Did you come by Shinkansen?
items.target: しんかんせんできましたか
items.pronunciation: shinkansen de kimashita ka
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Particle job (で): every existing で card is non-past or a bare fragment, so nothing asks about means of travel in the past.

items.english: Tanaka-san went home by motorbike.
items.target: たなかさんはバイクでうちにかえりました
items.pronunciation: Tanaka-san wa baiku de uchi ni kaerimashita
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Vocabulary job: バイク has no sentence card. Pairs the new noun with かえります so the transport list is not tied to いきます alone.
items.note: バイク (baiku) is a motorbike despite the English it comes from — the bicycle is じてんしゃ (jitensha).

items.english: Pak-san went to the airport by car.
items.target: パクさんはくるまでくうこうにいきました
items.pronunciation: Paku-san wa kuruma de kūkō ni ikimashita
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Vocabulary job: くるま has no sentence card. パク is one of the lesson's own three surnames and is used on no card at all.

items.english: How does Kato-san come to the office?
items.target: かとうさんはなんでかいしゃにきますか
items.pronunciation: Katō-san wa nande kaisha ni kimasu ka
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Form job: なんで attached to きます rather than いきます, which no card shows. Also the question half that gives でんしゃ its first sentence.
items.note: なんで (nande) also means "why" in casual speech, so なにで (nani de) is used when the sentence could be taken either way.

items.english: Emma-san went to Ginza by subway.
items.target: エマさんはちかてつでぎんざにいきました
items.pronunciation: Ema-san wa chikatetsu de Ginza ni ikimashita
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Vocabulary job: ちかてつ has no sentence card. Uses ぎんざ from Lesson 6 so the destination is familiar and the new word is the only load.

items.english: Pak-san isn't coming to Japan on Thursday.
items.target: パクさんはもくようびににほんにきません
items.pronunciation: Paku-san wa mokuyōbi ni Nihon ni kimasen
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Form job: negative member of the きます triad, a genuine hole — the deck teaches きます and きました but never the negative.
items.note: Member 2 of the set. きません (kimasen) appears on no other card, though its partner いきません (ikimasen) does.

items.english: From when to when is the business trip?
items.target: しゅっちょうはいつからいつまでですか
items.pronunciation: shutchō wa itsu kara itsu made desu ka
items.reviewNote: Constructed from the Exercise II.C pattern. Particle job (から / まで): only one card in the lesson uses them, and しゅっちょう — the word the Target Dialogue turns on — appears in no dated sentence.

items.english: No, we're going by Shinkansen.
items.target: いいえ、しんかんせんでいきます
items.pronunciation: iie, shinkansen de ikimasu
items.reviewNote: Target Dialogue, Smith's second reply — the line the lesson is named after. Answer half of the pair with hikouki-de-ikimasu-ka. Distinct from ks2-smith-shinkansen, which is a third-person statement naming the destination.
items.scene: answering whether you are going by airplane

items.english: Lopez-san is going to the station by bicycle.
items.target: ロペスさんはじてんしゃでえきにいきます
items.pronunciation: Ropesu-san wa jitensha de eki ni ikimasu
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Vocabulary job: じてんしゃ has no sentence card. Non-past, to balance the two past-tense transport sentences beside it.

items.english: Which bus goes to the airport?
items.target: どのバスがくうこうにいきますか
items.pronunciation: dono basu ga kūkō ni ikimasu ka
items.reviewNote: Duplicate of ga-dono-basu-ga-kuukou-ni-ikimasu-ka in Lesson 6. Its answer card carries a hint and stands alone.
items.note: A どの (dono) question asks which one of several, so the subject takes が (ga) rather than は (wa).

items.english: The festival is from the 1st to the 3rd.
items.target: おまつりはついたちからみっかまでです
items.pronunciation: omatsuri wa tsuitachi kara mikka made desu
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Vocabulary job: ついたち and みっか are bare cards with no sentence, and the irregular native readings are the ones worth drilling in context.
items.note: ついたち (tsuitachi) is the odd one out among the dates — it is not built from いち (ichi) at all.

items.english: Smith-san went home yesterday.
items.target: スミスさんはきのううちにかえりました
items.pronunciation: Sumisu-san wa kinō uchi ni kaerimashita
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Particle job (に vs no particle): member 2 of the minimal pair with w2-smith-nichiyoubi-ni-kaerimashita. Same sentence, same tense, only the time word swapped.
items.note: きのう (kinō) is a relative time word — it points at a day without naming one, and it never takes に (ni).

items.english: Is the trip in February or in March?
items.target: りょこうは2がつですか、3がつですか
items.pronunciation: ryokō wa ni-gatsu desu ka, san-gatsu desu ka
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Vocabulary job: にがつ and さんがつ had no sentence. Deliberately reuses the alternative-question form on months, since the existing examples of it are all days or clock times.
items.ttsText: りょこうはにがつですか、さんがつですか

items.english: No, I came by airplane.
items.target: いいえ、ひこうきできました
items.pronunciation: iie, hikōki de kimashita
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Particle job (で): answer half of the pair with w2-shinkansen-de-kimashita-ka, and the past-tense counterpart of the いいえ、しんかんせんでいきます pattern.
items.scene: answering whether you came by Shinkansen
